title: Striker Noonan agrees to join Forest
description: Michael Noonan will join Nottingham Forest on 1 January next year.
fullText:
Young striker Michael Noonan will join Nottingham Forest from Shamrock Rovers next year.

The 18-year-old has penned a pre-contract agreement and will officially move to the City Ground on 1 January.

Noonan has scored eight times for Shamrock this season, with Rovers second in the League of Ireland.

The forward also played in five of Shamrock's European games in the Champions League and Conference League qualifiers

His goal against Molde in February 2025 made him the youngest scorer in the Conference League's history and the second youngest in a Uefa club competition.

Chief Football Officer, George Syrianos, said: "Michael is a player we, along with a number of other clubs, have followed closely for some time, so we're delighted he has chosen Nottingham Forest.

"Recruiting high-potential young players is central to our long-term vision for the academy. We want the academy to be a genuine pathway to the first team, and that means bringing in the right talent early and giving them a clear, individual plan to get there.

"We look forward to welcoming Michael and his family to Forest and to supporting his development in the years ahead."

title: Barcelona superstar’s ridiculous start to the season is leaving Europe in awe
description: Barcelona have had an incredible start to the season, winning every game so far and scoring goals for fun in both La Liga and the Champions League.Among their many superstars, Lamine Yamal has started...
fullText:
Barcelona have had an incredible start to the season, winning every game so far and scoring goals for fun in both La Liga and the Champions League.

Among their many superstars, Lamine Yamal has started the new season at a frightening pace, with the Barcelona star producing 18 direct goal contributions across his first 10 official appearances for club and country.

The teenage superstar has 11 goals and seven assists across 829 minutes for Barcelona and Spain.

18 goal contributions in 10 matches works out at 1.8 per appearance, but Lamine's influence extends beyond the numbers.

He has produced 38 key passes and created 13 big chances while completing 39 dribbles. Those numbers capture what Lamine creates beyond goals and assists.

Lamine Yamal has been putting up absurd numbers since the start of the season. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images)

There is also significant defensive involvement. He has registered 30 recoveries and 22 defensive actions across those 10 appearances.

That matters under Hansi Flick. Individual brilliance will always define Lamine, but becoming more complete without the ball makes him even more valuable to the German manager.

His latest performance for Spain against Croatia has only increased the attention.

Lamine scored twice and provided an assist, and Europe has sat up and taken notice of his blistering start to the season.

All this makes even more sense when the Ballon d'Or comes into the picture. Lamine has been making a strong case to win the award, but the voting has now closed.

Lamine is in the reckoning for the Ballon d'Or this year. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

While last night's performance may not have influenced the voters in any way, his start to the season will surely have been a key factor.

The most exciting part is that Lamine is no longer producing spectacular moments without consistent output. He is combining both.

Eleven goals, seven assists, 38 key passes and 39 successful dribbles in only 10 games represent elite production even for a 29-year-old.

Sustaining these numbers will be a huge challenge, and it remains to be seen how Lamine fares in the coming weeks and months for Barça and La Roja.

title: Yaxel Lendeborg Impresses Stephen Curry, Al Horford At First Day Of Training Camp
description: Stephen Curry and Al Horford shared a glowing review of Yaxel Lendeborg after the first day of the Warriors' training camp.
fullText:
The Golden State Warriors' offseason was relatively underwhelming, primarily because it was marked by the front office's failure to recruit a superstar to pair with Stephen Curry. Still, calling it a failure may be unreasonable, as the Warriors added promising young pieces like Yaxel Lendeborg to the team's core.

Yaxel Lendeborg is likely to be one of the most intriguing players to follow on the Warriors' roster in the upcoming season. At 23, Lendeborg isn't a traditional rookie in need of physical development. As a player who can hit the ground running, the Michigan product is expected to make a big impact.

This aspect was acknowledged by Warriors veterans like Stephen Curry and Al Horford, who shared glowing reviews of Yaxel Lendeborg's potential after the first day of training camp. While speaking about his ability to contribute even as a rookie, Curry commented:

"I don't know; I mean, the expectation for him is just to keep getting better. The nature of our league and social media, all the microscopes, is that they're going to expect him to be a 20-8-6 guy right out the gate or whatever number you put on him. His job is to block all that out."

"You'll know; he'll know if he's impactful, he'll know if he's helping win games. The stats and the numbers will follow, and it's our job to protect him in that. But he also needs to have some confidence coming in that he can impact the game, and he establishes his own kind of metric of what a good game is. And just allow him to grow into that. He's going to get opportunities, though, so that's going to be fun."

Yaxel Lendeborg showcased his versatility at the Las Vegas Summer League, posting the 14.8 points, 6.7 rebounds, 4.0 assists, 1.3 steals, and 0.8 blocks per game, to help Golden State lift the Summer League trophy.

While the stats may not be the ideal metric to gauge his impact on the game, Curry emphasized that the veterans would have to shore him up from the media pressure to aid his development.

To garner such comments from a four-time NBA champion like Stephen Curry suggests that the rookie made a strong first impression. On that note, Curry even shared his early opinions of Lendeborg, stating:

"He's obviously a winner. You don't have the success that he had in college and the big role he had without that mentality. He's got great feel. He's obviously got great size. He was shooting really well. You can tell he wants to make the right play, and for our offense, and I mean our whole game plan, that's usually going to shine when you're seeing the floor, making good decisions."

Curry also praised the 23-year-old's open-mindedness, curiosity, and willingness to learn. However, it was Lendeborg's confidence to bounce back after making mistakes that really stood out to the 38-year-old, a trait that could be attributed to the forward's easygoing personality.

"He's super easy to be around," Curry continued. "He's very aware of his rookie duties, and he's also kind of making his presence felt, staying out of the way at the same time and just playing basketball. I don't really have to say much to him in that respect. Just try to be professional, do his job, and be a good presence in the locker room however he sees fit."

While Stephen Curry's comments on Yaxel Lendeborg primarily deal with his personality and how the rookie fits the team's complex offensive system, Warriors veteran Al Horford shared key observations about how Lendeborg could be impactful on defense.

"I think that Coach Vogel has been pretty clear on how he wants us to play defense, where we need to be, and defense a lot of the time," Horford began.

"It's all about positioning; it's all about communication. So, for [Yaxel], we're staying on him about making sure that he's communicating, making sure that he's in the right position, and if he's able to do those things, I feel like he will find his way. But it all sounds good until we start playing. He has to be able to show that he can hold his own defensively."

While Yaxel Lendeborg's laid-back attitude has helped him break the ice with his teammates, even earning some praise from Curry, the rookie clearly has his work cut out for him on defense.

Since Yaxel Lendeborg is expected to step up and be a two-way threat for the Warriors, he must learn to be disciplined on the defensive end, especially if he is to be paired with the likes of Draymond Green and Al Horford.

Even in light of the positive reviews from the veterans, the 23-year-old will be put through the wringer this training camp period. Still, if things play out according to the Warriors' plans, he could quickly emerge as one of the most vital players on the roster.

title: Re-ranking NASCAR Chase drivers: Kyle Larson is the new favorite
description: Heading into Las Vegas, the fifth race of NASCAR's postseason, Kyle Larson looks like the favorite to win the Chase. But don't count out Penske yet.
fullText:
Four races are in the books in NASCAR's postseason Chase. With six weekends remaining, the championship picture is becoming clearer.

Larson, who won championships in 2021 and 2025, had an up-and-down start to the season with nine finishes of 30th or worse. Three of those were DNFs, and he was riding a 51-race winless streak until he took the checkered flag at Gateway on Sept. 13.

After winning at Kansas last weekend, Larson is now the driver everyone else is chasing.

"I consider Kyle Larson one of the greatest race drivers I've ever seen perform anywhere in the world, but I didn't see this coming at all," Hall of Fame driver and USA Network analyst Dale Jarrett told USA TODAY Sports recently. "That's a testament to Hendrick Motorsports, to Kyle Larson, to (crew chief) Cliff Daniels. It's shocking, but I'm not surprised it's Kyle Larson that we're talking about that has made this great run because I think he's just so tremendously talented.

"He has set the standard now and he has applied a tremendous amount of pressure to the contenders that were ahead of him, but now looking up at him at the top of the board."

Hamlin, still searching for his first Cup Series championship at the age of 45, has held serve in the last three Chase races after a rough 18th place finish at Darlington. He placed inside the top 10 at Gateway and Bristol, then ran third this past weekend at Kansas. But to catch Larson, Hamlin is going to have to remain consistent, or hope Larson has a bad day. Winning a race for the first time since June 14 at Pocono would go a long way too.

Other drivers have faded back in the standings and simply have too much ground in front of them to make up. Others, like Team Penske drivers Joey Logano and Ryan Blaney, need to tread water through this stretch of the postseason until the Chase returns to tracks more favorable to their Fords.

And then there's Tyler Reddick, once seen as the championship favorite who hasn't been able to find consistency in the second half of the season.

"We got big problems," Reddick told reporters after an 11th place finish at Kansas. "We just got to figure out our own (expletive) right now. … Even if I had to imagine when our car was at its best (at Kansas) it still wasn't great. We're still off."

With six races remaining, USA TODAY Sports presents tier rankings for each of the 16 drivers' chances to win the Chase:

All of these drivers are at least 150 points behind the leader and haven't shown the consistency this season that's required to make up that much ground in just six races. Suarez, Preece, Elliott and Hocevar have all won races this season, but aside from Hocevar's eventful night at Bristol, none of them have challenged for a win in the Chase yet – and Hocevar followed that up with a dreadful run at Kansas where he finished three laps down.

Wallace was having a solid day at Kansas until he was collected in a multi-car wreck on a restart. Cindric and Briscoe both challenged Larson for the lead, but ultimately couldn't pass him for the checkered flag. This trio of drivers have shown the ability to string together good races, but they need to start piling up points to have a chance of catching the contenders. If one of them has a bad run at Las Vegas, it's curtains for their championship hopes.

Reddick won five of the first nine races of the season, but has since been plagued by pit road problems, issues under the hood or bad luck. He finished third at Darlington, but hasn't cracked the top 10 since. Beginning with a DNF at Michigan in early June, Reddick just hasn't been able to recreate the success he had early in the season.

Gibbs has won two races this season, at Bristol and Iowa, but hasn't strung together back-to-back top-10 finishes since mid-July. An average finish of 13.8 over his last seven races isn't going to cut it in the Chase.

The pair of Team Penske teammates need to have mistake-free races and solid finishes over the next two stops in the Chase, Las Vegas and Charlotte. While Penske wasn't all that good on mile-and-a-half tracks early in the season, the team and Ford seemed to have figured something out as Blaney placed fifth at Kansas and teammate Austin Cindric ran second.

A win at either Las Vegas or Charlotte would be huge for the championship hopes of Blaney or Logano – and indeed, Blaney won at Charlotte in 2023 and Logano has four career victories at Las Vegas – but these two drivers mostly just need to stay within striking distance heading into the final four races: Phoenix, Talladega, Martinsville and Homestead.

Penske Fords have been strong at short tracks all year, evidenced by Blaney's win at Phoenix in the spring and Logano's run of wins at North Wilkesboro, Richmond and Bristol. Logano and Blaney also each have three wins apiece at Talladega, a superspeedway where anything can happen.

The contenders should be worried if either driver remains in the mix entering the final four races.

Larson has two wins in the Chase, Bell got a win at Darlington and has two other top-10 finishes, and Hamlin has been the most consistent driver this season with zero DNFs while also leading the field in top-10 finishes and top-five finishes.

Hamlin has won the last two races at Las Vegas, while Larson has three victories at the track in his career. Bell – who is 50 points behind Larson – has placed inside the top five at Las Vegas in five of his last seven races there.

This Sunday is shaping up to be a race where the contenders could be battling for what would be a crucial win.

title: France midfielder Koné 'shocked' by coach Zidane's ability in training
description: France midfielder Manu Koné had to pinch himself when new coach Zinedine Zidane laced up his boots to take part in training.  Arguably the world’s best playmaker during his heyday, the 54-year-old Zidane was in his element spraying passes around and whipping in crosses to his awe-struck players.  “Seeing it in person is even better, especially at his age,” the 25-year-old Koné added.
fullText:
PARIS (AP) — France midfielder Manu Koné had to pinch himself when new coach Zinedine Zidane laced up his boots to take part in training.

Arguably the world's best playmaker during his heyday, the 54-year-old Zidane was in his element spraying passes around and whipping in crosses to his awe-struck players.

"What shocked me during the first week of training was his technical range. He's lost none of his ability," Koné said on Tuesday ahead of Friday's game against Italy at Stade de France in the Nations League.

"Seeing it in person is even better, especially at his age," the 25-year-old Koné added. "It's true that I was little when he was near the end of his career. To see that he still has that technique now means it must have been incredible in his era."

Zidane's two goals in the 1998 World Cup final win against Brazil made him an overnight superstar, with his face famously beamed on the Arc de Triomphe in Paris as a nation celebrated. A Ballon d'Or award followed and, two years later, his superb performances led Les Bleus to more glory at the European Championship.

"It's a pleasure to be coached by Zidane, a world legend. He's told me to play freely and given me confidence," Koné added. "He was a midfielder, so as a midfielder I listen to everything he says and I can only learn by his side. He advises me a lot about my positioning and gives me more responsibility."

Zidane's last performance for France was in the 2006 World Cup final, which ended in a penalty shootout loss to Italy. Even though Zidane was sent off in extra time for head-butting Italy defender Marco Materazzi when France was dominating, it did not affect his popularity among French soccer fans.

Since his arrival Zidane has been in the spotlight even more than some of the stars in his squad.

"We shouldn't be shocked, you can only congratulate him for his career," Koné said. "We will see that on Friday, the ovation he gets (against Italy)."

Zidane played Koné in a sentry midfield role in a 1-0 win at Turkey last Friday, which meant largely sitting in front of and protecting the defense with limited scope to push up.

Two weeks ago, Koné scored twice for Roma against Inter Milan in a table-topping Serie A clash but has yet to find the net in 21 appearances for Les Bleus.

"The goal will come," he said. "But the important thing is to meet the coach's requirements." ___

title: Baldini reacts to Kayode’s Italy debut: ‘All of my U21 players can make the step up’
description: Italy U21 head coach Silvio Baldini hopes that Michael Kayode is not the only youngster to break into the senior national team squad in the near future, promising that “all of my players can make th...
fullText:
Italy U21 head coach Silvio Baldini hopes that Michael Kayode is not the only youngster to break into the senior national team squad in the near future, promising that "all of my players can make the step up".

Brentford right-back Kayode was the standout performer, providing a goal and an assist on his debut, as Italy beat Turkey 4-1 to claim their first win of Roberto Mancini's second spell in charge on Monday night.

BURSA, TURKEY – SEPTEMBER 28: Michael Kayode of Italy celebrates scoring his team's third goal with teammate Sandro Tonali during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Türkiye and Italy at Atatürk Spor Kompleksi Matli Stadyumu on September 28, 2026 in Bursa, Turkey. (Photo by Ahmad Mora/Getty Images)

Not only was the Turkey game Kayode's first cap, this is only his first camp with the Italy national team squad, despite an impressive individual and collective season with Brentford in the Premier League in 2025-26.

His former Italy U21 coach Baldini, who is preparing to lead the Azzurrini into a crucial EURO U21 qualifier against Armenia on Thursday evening, was asked about Kayode's impressive Nazionale debut during his pre-match press conference on Wednesday, promising that there could be several other players to follow in the near future.

"All of my players can make the step up," Baldini told the press (via TMW).

"We were happy with the victory the other night, we saw a new atmosphere. It's a new cycle that could start well and we hope to see a great performance against France as well."

EMPOLI – MARCH 26: Silvio Baldini manager of Italy U21 looks on during the UEFA Under 21 EURO Qualifier match between Italy U21 and North Macedonia U21 at Stadio Carlo Castellani on March 26, 2026 in Empoli. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images)

Speaking at the start of the international break last week, Baldini hinted that Roberto Mancini could call up several of his Italy U21 players for the next international break in November. He also hinted that Mancini was already considering calling several of them up for the September-October break, but that they were left with the U21s ahead of a crucial pair of EUROs qualifiers.

"Mancini knows this group very well. He knows which players could be useful to him, and I think that he's left several of them with us because we have these important qualifying matches to play. So, maybe during the next break some of the guys who are here today could be with the senior national team."

CREMONA – OCTOBER 14: Coach Silvio Baldini of Italy reacts during the UEFA Euro U21 Qualification match between Italy and Armenia at Stadio Giovanni Zini on October 14, 2025 in Cremona. (Photo by Marco M. Mantovani/Getty Images)

Midfielders: Cher Ndour (Fiorentina), Niccolo Pisilli (Roma), Luca Lipani (Sassuolo), Giacomo Faticanti (Avellino), Tommaso Berti (Cremonese), Matteo Cichella (Frosinone).

title: Integrity brought into question of undisclosed people associated with Man City
description: "To cheat, trick, deceive, delude with false pretences; to impose upon, take in, hoax."  It is a word that appears eight times in the independent commission's ruling, published on Tuesday, which found Manchester City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of financial rules - and all but one in relation to a failure to co-operate with the investigation.  It catalogues how the club's owners, Abu Dhabi United Group, knew from the 2009-10 season that there would be major overspends if the club was to reach the level they wanted to get to.
fullText:
"To cheat, trick, deceive, delude with false pretences; to impose upon, take in, hoax." That is the Oxford English definition of the word 'sham'.

It is a word that appears eight times in the independent commission's ruling, published on Tuesday, which found Manchester City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of financial rules - and all but one in relation to a failure to co-operate with the investigation.

The 40-page document makes fascinating reading.

It catalogues how the club's owners, Abu Dhabi United Group, knew from the 2009-10 season that there would be major overspends if the club was to reach the level they wanted to get to.

So, the ruling says, Manchester City found a way to boost sponsorship income - season, after season, after season. For nine seasons, in fact.

These were ambitious new owners who didn't just want the club to be competitive, they also wanted to have the best players and to be winners. That wasn't going to be possible without spending more money, and lots of it.

Total losses for the 2009-10 campaign were going to exceed what was, at that time, the record single-season financial loss by a Premier League member club. That was previously set at £140m by Chelsea in 2006.

According to the ruling, that was a record that Manchester City's owners were adamant the club should not break.

And, not only that, but the club knew they would likely continue to suffer large losses for at least the following five seasons.

This was when both Uefa and the Premier League were about to bring in financial fair play rules, so it was clearly going to be a problem.

To address this, the only option was to significantly increase commercial revenue and reduce the reliance on their owners.

"The club made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the Premier League investigation," the independent commission's ruling continued.

It is another damning section which brings into question the integrity of undisclosed people associated with Manchester City.

The club served witness statements or documentary evidence from 24 individuals, most of whom who gave evidence at the hearing.

At present, no one has been named so we don't know the positions of the people the ruling referred to. However, it said the evidence given by a number of important factual witnesses "was false in a number of key respects".

The ruling also said that Manchester City knew their annual accounts "did not provide a true and fair view of the financial position" and the club "was reckless as to whether those annual accounts provided a true and fair view".

All of this, it was said, showed the club failed to act "with utmost good faith" and "breached duties of co-operation that it owed to the Premier League".

title: Liberty make WNBA history by stunning No. 1 Lynx in playoff sweep
description: A stunning WNBA result in the first round of the playoffs.
fullText:
Liberty make WNBA history by stunning No. 1 Lynx in playoff sweep originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The biggest upset of the WNBA playoffs is complete.

And it was historic. The eighth-seeded New York Liberty eliminated the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx with an 87-71 victory Tuesday night, completing a stunning 2-0 sweep.

New York became the first No. 8 seed to eliminate a No. 1 seed in WNBA playoff history.

For Minnesota, a season built around championship expectations ended almost immediately. For New York, the postseason suddenly looks completely different.

New York's biggest names weren't interested in extending the series. Jonquel Jones finished with 21 points and 13 rebounds. Breanna Stewart added 21 points, while Sabrina Ionescu contributed 18 points and seven assists.

LIBERTY SWEEP LYNX TO BECOME THE FIRST NO. 8 SEED TO KNOCK OFF THE NO. 1 SEED IN WNBA HISTORY 🚨🤯 pic.twitter.com/bUagjVRhB5

That may be the most surprising element of the entire result.

Minnesota entered the postseason as the league's top seed, yet New York dictated Game 2 from the beginning. This wasn't a last-second escape. It was a decisive elimination game.

MORE: Caitlin Clark's spectacular pass showed what the Fever need more of against the Aces

That's the danger of postseason basketball.

Regular-season accomplishments establish expectations. They don't guarantee anything once elimination games begin.

Minnesota discovered that in brutal fashion. New York entered the playoffs as the No. 8 seed following an uneven regular season, but the Liberty still possessed a roster filled with players accustomed to major postseason moments.

Now New York moves into the semifinals after pulling off something no eighth seed had previously accomplished against a No. 1 seed in league playoff history.

The Liberty will face the winner of the Atlanta Dream-Washington Mystics series.

Suddenly, the team that barely made its way into the postseason has become one of its biggest stories.

Minnesota is going home. New York is moving on.

And the WNBA playoffs have already delivered a result that will be remembered long after this postseason ends.

title: WNBA clarifies why A’ja Wilson got a technical foul after Fever altercation
description: Following the Aces’ intense matchup against the Fever, the WNBA released its official pool report to explain the A’ja Wilson call. fullText:
Following the Aces' intense matchup against the Fever, the WNBA released its official pool report to explain the A'ja Wilson call.

A'ja Wilson found herself right in the middle of standard WNBA chaos during Game 2, getting hit with a technical foul after a fan stepped toward her and pointed.

Indiana capitalised on the home-court energy, pulling off a 99-89 win to knot their playoff series at 1-1.

Postgame, Wilson didn't hold back about the fan being allowed to stay in his seat, calling the behavior unacceptable and stating, "You don't step towards me and point at me—I'm not for that at all".

According to the official WNBA pool report following the September 29, 2026 game between Las Vegas and Indiana, crew chief Randy Richardson addressed the sideline incident involving A'ja Wilson and a fan.

When asked twice about what went down and why the whistle blew, Richardson kept it simple and direct: Wilson was given a technical foul strictly for unsportsmanlike conduct stemming from her interaction with that fan on the baseline. Basically, the officiating crew determined her reaction crossed the line into unsportsmanlike territory, regardless of whatever went back and forth between her and the crowd.

However, one thing that doesn't make much sense is the fact that it states it was an 'interaction with the fan on the baseline', which is slightly inaccurate, as Wilson went into row two to address the fan.

title: Guernsey's pride as Scott wins first England cap
description: Guernsey has "a lot of pride" after Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott made his England debut.
fullText:
Guernsey has "a lot of pride" for Alex Scott after the Bournemouth midfielder made his England debut.

The 23-year-old came on as a second-half substitute in England's 2-0 win over the Czech Republic in the Nations League on Tuesday night.

He became just the second footballer from Guernsey to play for England's men's side after former Southampton striker Matt Le Tissier.

He joins his step-sister, Manchester United's Maya Le Tissier, in becoming an international for England.

"There's a lot of pride for every Guernseyman that's watching him," Guernsey FC manager Tony Vance told BBC Radio Guernsey.

Having left Southampton's academy as a young teenager Scott returned to his home island and played for Vance's team who were then in the eighth tier Isthmian League South Central league.

Alex Scott - the 'Guernsey boy' playing for England

Youngster Scott impresses Guernsey boss

He made his debut aged 16 and is still the club's youngest-ever player, before being picked up by Bristol City where he made 91 appearances before joining Premier League AFC Bournemouth in 2023.

"It's incredible that when you look at that and then obviously Maya as well, so for a small island we do punch above our weight," added Vance.

"In Guernsey we know all the players coming through from a very early age and obviously Alex was a standout and everyone knew about that.

"He had some setbacks early in his career and he came back a little bit lost.

"Luckily we managed to get him back into the frame a bit and it was obvious it wasn't going to be long that he was going to be with us, he just kept pushing and pushing.

"He's in a pretty strong position now but it's not without any hard work and a lot of pain, but he deserves everything he's got and so do his family."

Scott became the 1,301st player to play for England when he came on at the Fortuna Arena.

It is something that he says will live with him forever, and a bright moment in a difficult time after the recent passing of his grandfather.

"It's what dreams are made of and something that probably when I was younger and maybe even 15 or 16 wasn't wasn't a reality at all," Scott told BBC Radio 5live

"I've worked really hard and it's a proud moment for me of course, and my family as well.

"I had no nerves at all really, I was more nervous for the speech to the lads after the game.

"I was just obviously happy to get my opportunity, I've been on a few camps now, I know the boys pretty well and the staff as well so it was great for me to finally get on the pitch."

Scott is one of a number of young players from Guernsey that are playing professionally off the island.

Midfielder Joe Adams is at Wigan Athletic, while Jack Griffin is part of Bristol City's academy, Chloe Ingrouille is in Plymouth Argyle's women's set-up and triplets Emilie, Hollie and Millie Jeffreys have all joined York City.

Vance feels that Scott's journey is one that can inspire even more Guernsey players to try and make it in the game.

"There are going to be some other players that hopefully will get to professional football, maybe not to the extremes Alex has got to," he said.

"But ultimately he is the aspiration and the inspiration to every youngster now and it's an example for us to say 'there's the pathway'.

"A few others have made professional football from it, but he's achieved the ultimate dream and that's to play for England and that's incredible."

title: Bayern Munich set to offer Michael Olise new long-term contract to deter interest from other clubs

fullText:
Bayern Munich are set to offer French international attacking midfielder Michael Olise (24) a new long-term contract to extend his stay with the club, according to a report from BILD. The Bundesliga giants are aiming to retain the services of the former Crystal Palace playmaker and deter interest from other clubs after a summer transfer window fuelled with rumours regarding his long-term future in Bavaria.

Real Madrid were at the front of the queue to sign the 24-year-old during the summer transfer window. However, with Bayern refusing to negotiate with the La Liga outfit, the Spanish capital club were forced to look elsewhere to reinforce the options of Jose Mourinho. PSG were also linked with a move for the Frenchman. Even now the window has closed, the rumour mill continues to link the attacking midfielder with a move away from Germany.

In a bid to extend the attacker's stay in the Bundesliga, Bayern Munich are preparing to offer Olise a contract extension with a substantial pay rise. If the Chelsea academy graduate was to accept the terms, this would extend his stay in Bavaria for a further 6 years. His current contract is set to expire in 2029.

Geno Smith and the New York Jets only have a win to show for three weeks of action, but one can make a strong case that they should be among the few undefeated teams left to date in the 2026 NFL regular season.

Smith has been more or less steady under center in his second stint with New York. So far in the 2026 campaign, the former West Virginia Mountaineers star quarterback has thrown for 783 passing yards and four touchdowns against zero interceptions. The 35-year-old QB has been holding his own; though, he has also been sacked nine times already.

Still, he is seemingly exceeding expectations.

In fact, he posted a 75.5 percent completion rate over the first three weeks, the highest in the history of the Jets franchise over the same span, as announced by the team on X.

hot start for @GenoSmith3 pic.twitter.com/Erscq4WUFo

— New York Jets (@nyjets) September 29, 2026

The Jets selected Smith in the third round of the 2013 NFL Draft, but his first stint with the team never worked out. He later found his way into the New York Giants before rediscovering his form and confidence with the Seattle Seahawks. With the Seahawks, he earned two Pro Bowl nods and even won Comeback Player honors in 2022.

This time, Smith is looking to bounce back after a forgettable one-year stay with the Las Vegas Raiders in 2025.

The Jets have shown some fight this season, but they failed to get it together over the past two weeks, losing to the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions by a combined margin of 10 points.

Up ahead for New York is a date with the Chicago Bears on Sunday at Soldier Field.

fullText:
The Philadelphia Eagles are picking up the pieces following an embarrassing loss in a Monday Night Football loss to the Chicago Bears.

The defeat was certainly not a good look on Philly, especially since the Bears did not even have Week 1 starter Caleb Williams in the game due to a hamstring injury.

Instead, it was veteran quarterback and journeyman Case Keenum who led the way for Chicago, which came away with a 27-7 win at Soldier Field in Chicago.

It was the first loss of the season for the Eagles, which defeated the Washington Commanders at home in Week 1 and the Tennessee Titans on the road in Week 2.

Chicago perhaps represented the first true test for the Eagles this season, and they failed in it, leaving a bad taste in their mouth.

Philadelphia allowed Keenum and the Bears to compile 375 total yards, while the Eagles only had 248. Philly also turned the ball over three times to zero from Chicago.

The crushing loss to Chicago also did damage to Philadelphia's standing in several power rankings, including on the NFL's official website. The Eagles entered Week 3 ranked 10th, but are now 15th.

Here's what is said about Philly on the rankings:

The Eagles failed their first real test of 2026 in a fashion that suggested they didn't even take time to study. Jalen Hurts struggled for most of the night, Philadelphia wasted a promising, Saquon Barkley-heavy drive by throwing an interception in the end zone, and the defense surrendered 375 yards to a Case Keenum-led offense. The Eagles' offensive evolution under Sean Mannion hasn't yet taken hold (Hurts didn't help with that much on Monday night), and right now, I'm not exactly sure how to feel about this team. Philly should be good, but through three weeks, it has logged two narrow wins over teams it's expected to beat, and lost a lopsided game on the road. Not great, Nick (Sirianni)!

Hurts and company can turn things around quickly in their next game, against the Los Angeles Rams at home in Week 4.

title: Wiegman explains why Chloe Kelly was dropped by England
description: Sarina Wiegman has explained why Chloe Kelly was left out of the latest England squad, with the decision coming before the forward’s current hamstring problem.Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty ImagesSarina...
fullText:
Sarina Wiegman has explained why Chloe Kelly was left out of the latest England squad, with the forward omitted before the hamstring problem that has since ruled her out for Arsenal.

Kelly was absent from open training at London Colney on Tuesday as Arsenal prepared for their Champions League game against Paris FC on Wednesday evening.

Asked about her absence after the session, Renée Slegers confirmed that Kelly was managing a hamstring problem, prompting speculation that it had been behind her England omission.

"She's had some issues with her hamstring and no injury," Slegers told reporters. "Nothing we could see from an injury perspective, but been managing something, and at the moment, not available to play."

Slegers was then asked whether that was why Kelly had not been selected by England, but made clear that it was not.

"I think Sarina's had a press conference this morning and that's between England and the player of course," she replied.

"That's their decisions. I don't know exactly what's being communicated in that moment, but of course that's Sarina's decision. Yes, so she played, I think England announced her squad today, she played on Sunday, she played 30-plus minutes for us, so at that point she was fit and available."

At her own press conference, Wiegman was asked about leaving out Kelly and Ella Toone of Manchester United.

"The main reason is that I think the levels weren't what I expected from them on the pitch," Wiegman said of the two omissions," the England head coach said.

"I've had a conversation with them and there's a big competition going on too.

"Of course that has been a very hard decision for both of them. I really believe in them and we follow them really well, and we expect a bit more. And we know they can bring more. And that was the message again too."

Kelly has now been ruled out of Arsenal's game in Paris and, with a hamstring still troubling her, a few weeks away from international duty may at least give her time to recover.

Slegers was also asked how Arsenal can help the 28-year-old return to her best.

"Yeah, that was an amazing second half of the season and it was fantastic to see what happened with Chloe coming back to Arsenal and how she connected with the fans, with the club," Slegers said about Kelly when she first signed on loan from Manchester City in January 2025.

"So, a very special moment and then on top of that winning the Champions League.

"Of course it's number one, starting point for a player is always to be fit and available, that's where it starts and then if you look at the squad that we have right now, it's also about competing for playing minutes and she's doing that.

"But like I said, at the moment, not fully fit and hopefully she gets back to her best soon."

title: Seven MLB players who played all 162 games in 2026
description: Every spring, dozens of players say they want to play every day. By the final Sunday of the 2026 regular season, only seven had actually done it, appearing in all 162 of their team’s games. The group mixes a record-chasing first baseman, a two-time MVP, a rookie and an MVP front-runner. Each took a different…
fullText:
Every spring, dozens of players say they want to play every day. By the final Sunday of the 2026 regular season, only seven had actually done it, appearing in all 162 of their team's games.

The group mixes a record-chasing first baseman, a two-time MVP, a rookie and an MVP front-runner. Each took a different path to the same number, and several got there for the first time in their careers.

Modern teams lean heavily on scheduled rest days, platoons and cautious injury management. That makes a full-season line on the stat sheet a rare badge, one that reflects health, trust from managers and a little luck.

Luck cut the other way for Baltimore's Pete Alonso. He played in 161 games, but the Orioles' Sept. 27 finale at Yankee Stadium was canceled by weather after a nearly three-hour delay, leaving no 162nd game to play.

Alonso still finished with an AL-leading 43 home runs and 113 RBIs. The seven who made it, however, start with a player who has turned showing up into a historic habit.

Atlanta's Matt Olson played every game for the fifth straight season. His consecutive games streak, which began May 2, 2021, with the Oakland Athletics, reached 944 games by the end of the year, according to The Associated Press.

That total pushes Olson past Stan Musial's 895 on the all-time list. On July 10, he also passed Dale Murphy for the longest streak in Braves franchise history, with his 741st straight game for Atlanta.

Olson has never treated the streak as a goal. "I just expect to play if I'm healthy and ready to go, and it's just kind of stacked up games," he told MLB.com after setting the franchise mark.

Two-time MVP Bryce Harper appeared in all 162 games for the first time in his 15-season MLB career. His previous high was 159 games with Washington in 2018. Before 2026, his only Philadelphia season above 145 games was 2019, when he played 157.

The 33-year-old Phillies star had spoken openly about his goal. "Obviously, it's in my head that I want to do it," Harper said in July, while emphasizing the importance of staying healthy and winning.

His final regular-season appearance carried playoff stakes. Harper homered in Philadelphia's 7-3 victory over Tampa Bay on September 27, clinching the final NL wild-card berth with an 88-74 record.

Matt Olson had company in the Braves' lineup throughout the regular season. Second baseman Ozzie Albies also appeared in all 162 games, a notable turnaround after injuries interrupted several recent seasons.

Albies broke his left foot in 2022 and fractured his left wrist in 2024, missing substantial time in both years. In 2026, he stayed on the field as Atlanta finished 94-68 and won the NL East.

The Braves improved by 18 wins over 2025, with their durable infielders providing a steady foundation. Atlanta opened its Wild Card Series against Philadelphia with a 5-3 victory on September 29.

On the other side of that game stood Tampa Bay's Junior Caminero, who made history of his own. He became just the fourth player since divisional play began in 1969 to start all 162 games at third base.

Caminero joined Sal Bando in 1969, Cal Ripken Jr. in 1997 and Vinny Castilla in 1998. Few positions are more physically demanding over a full season, which helps explain why the list is so short.

The 23-year-old paired that durability with production. He reached 40 home runs with a September walk-off that clinched a playoff berth and topped 100 RBIs for a second straight season on a 98-win Rays club.

Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong also played in all 162 games, and his season may carry the biggest award implications of the group. He is widely considered a leading candidate for NL MVP honors.

Crow-Armstrong tied Kyle Schwarber for the major league lead with 45 home runs, according to MLB.com's final stat leaders. He also led the NL with a .942 OPS and topped the majors with 10.6 WAR.

Earlier this season, he became only the second left-handed hitter in Cubs history to hit 40 home runs in a season, joining Hall of Famer Billy Williams. Doing it without a day off only adds to the case.

Cincinnati's Sal Stewart became the first rookie to appear in all 162 games since Delmon Young did it for Tampa Bay in 2007. Stewart started 161 games and made 1 appearance as a pinch-hitter.

He stayed in the lineup while playing first base, second base, and third base and also serving as a designated hitter. Stewart finished with 32 home runs and a Reds rookie record 111 RBIs.

The 22-year-old earned an All-Star selection during his rookie season. "I'm blessed. I had a great year, but I'm not satisfied," Stewart said, according to Sports Illustrated.

Pittsburgh's Bryan Reynolds became the first Pirates player to appear in all 162 games since Jason Bay in 2005.

Reynolds had approached that mark before, playing 159 games in 2021 and 156 in 2024. In 2026, he combined his durability with steady production, finishing with a major league-leading 40 doubles.

Pirates manager Don Kelly praised Reynolds's stability and consistency. Reynolds joined 6 other players in reaching 162 appearances during the regular season, earning a distinction that remains rare.

Fun fact: Olson's 944-game streak is impressive, but it's still well short of the record. Cal Ripken Jr. played in 2,632 consecutive games, the longest streak in MLB history.

Seven players appeared in all 162 games in 2026: Matt Olson, Ozzie Albies, Bryce Harper, Junior Caminero, Pete Crow-Armstrong, Sal Stewart, and Bryan Reynolds.

Olson's streak reached 944 games, passing Stan Musial on the all-time list.

Harper, Reynolds, and Albies reached 162 games for the first time.

Caminero became the fourth player since 1969 to start all 162 games at third base.

Stewart was the first rookie to play every game since 2007.

Pete Alonso played 161 after a rainout wiped out Baltimore's finale.

title: Is Harley-Davidson Done With King of the Baggers?
description: The Bar and Shielded brand could be looking more globally, and not just the States.
fullText:
King of the Baggers is one of those race series you've got to see in person, as nothing on TV or social media delivers the same visceral experience as a full grid of 700-pound behemoths race toward the first turn and, somehow, make it.  They're loud, they're obnoxious, and these gorillas somehow dance around as if they were petite ballerinas that weigh as much as their tutus.

This year's season was clinched by Indian Motorcycle, while last year's was taken by Harley-Davidson. And that's been the sort of off-and-on relationship to the championship since the series was founded about six years ago. Back and forth between the brands, though with factory and privateer teams also switching it up throughout. Again, this series is all about spectacle and noise and grunt and a rivalry—sometimes friendly, sometimes not—between these two distinctly American brands.

That, however, could all be coming to an end, as while Harley-Davidson hasn't declared what its intentions are for the 2027 season, its factory-backed riders seem to be hinting that the Motor Co. isn't returning to the grind come next year. And for American bagger fans, that'll be a gut punch, to say the least.

Ex-MotoGP Race Winner Fails To Secure FIM Bagger World Cup Title

Kyle Wyman, King of the Baggers, and How Racing Impacts Product Development

Now, myself and the rest of the internet could be reading too much into this. Again, Harley hasn't said what its plans are outright, and we all could be getting worked up for nothing. But I want you all to read Kyle Wyman's words, who is the lead Harley-Davidson x Dynojet Factory Race Team rider, which he gave at the end of the season at New Jersey Motorsports Park, in which Wyman came in 4th in the first race, and 1st in the second.

"This team has changed my life and changed my career. This one's going to feel really good for a long time," said Wyman, adding, "How can you sum up what we've done with this program? You just can't. We've created a lot of memories and impacted a lot of people in a positive way. I wouldn't want to do it with any other group. I want to give a huge thanks to Harley-Davidson, to all of our partners and our fans. The fans have been incredible. It's great to give them one more win."

The finality in his words seem prescient, don't you think? As if he's closing a chapter that he can't quite publicly state just yet, but undoubtedly knows is coming. Again, this also could be that Wyman is just closing out the season. But Road Race Report quoted Wyman's teammate Bradley Smith—who ended in P2 in the overall championship—as saying there were some changes coming that might require him to "look elsewhere for next year." It's unclear what he meant, but given he snatched second overall, I wouldn't imagine that Harley would be looking to outright replace him at the team.

That has led many to speculate that Harley-Davidson could be looking to just focus on its recently announced partnership with MotoGP and its recently introduced Bagger World Cup, a single-make series that's sponsored and raced exclusively by Harley-Davidson. And, honestly, it makes a lot of sense.

MotoGP's new owners, Liberty Media, are desperate to make waves here in the States with the series. Harley-Davidson is as iconic an American brand as you can get. Having them as a support series, and possibly giving them some further commercial time on air to bring in more Americans, could be a great move. Not only for MotoGP, but also for Harley-Davidson, which has been suffering abroad in recent years due to it being a tariff pawn in the great world economic game. Moreover, MotoGP, even its support series', have far larger audiences than motorcycle racing here in the States.

But again, nothing has been confirmed. Everything is rumors and gossip. Wyman and Smith's comments, however, are interesting to ponder, though.

title: Danica Patrick Sparks Debate Over Golf Course Behavior
description: Golf fans defend Danica Patrick after a viral photo shows her celebrating on the course, challenging traditional norms of etiquette and slow play.
fullText:
Golf culture often treats the course like a quiet sanctuary, but recent events suggest that line is blurring. A photo of Danica Patrick and her friends celebrating a round went viral on social media earlier this week, per Yahoo Sports. The image showed the group engaged in a bit of a dogpile, a stark contrast to the usual solemn walk off the final green.

While some traditionalists saw this as a breach of etiquette, others saw it as harmless fun. The reaction split the community immediately, with fans debating what actually counts as acceptable behavior during a round. The incident highlights a growing tension between old-school rules and modern expressions of joy on the links.

The core of the controversy stems from whether the group was actually slowing down the game. According to Yahoo Sports, some golf fans disliked the behavior, suggesting that Patrick and her friends were holding up play and acting inappropriately. However, a strong wave of support emerged quickly to defend the former NASCAR driver.

Many fans argued that the outrage was manufactured and unnecessary. One fan wrote, "Were the gals holding up play? If not- stop with the faux outrage at everything the gal does. It's not like they were wearing bikinis out there- sheesh!" This sentiment reflects a broader frustration with the rigid expectations placed on golfers, especially women.

Supporters also pointed out the hypocrisy of criticizing a celebratory moment while ignoring similar behavior from men. Another fan noted, "Golf courses are dirt, grass, sand, trees and water. Don't pretend like they're churches. Besides, how many photos of guys with stogies and beer posing on golf courses have there been taken? And what guy wouldn't want to be in the foursome behind them? I'd take the picture for them!"

The argument suggests that men often get a pass for boisterous conduct that draws criticism when women do it. One supporter even vented about the elitism of country clubs, stating, "Snot nosed country clubbers can go pack sand!!! They think their poo don't stink." The fan described how these same clubs complain about public access while allowing carts to be driven drunk on public streets at night.

The context of the photo matters too. It appears the celebration happened on the last hole. As one fan explained, "That was the last hole and I don't think people at the club she was playing are concerned with slow play." The fan added that the group likely just took a bit longer to let the people behind them tee off, a common occurrence.

They even mentioned a similar situation involving actor Kevin James playing a round at Royal, implying that such moments are standard for high-profile guests. Reports confirm that the photo sparked a divide, with some seeing disrespect and others seeing a natural, relaxing moment that anyone should be allowed to have.

The backlash against Danica Patrick reveals a deeper issue in how the game polices itself. Golf has long relied on an unwritten code of conduct that prioritizes silence and speed above all else. But this code often feels less like a rulebook and more like a gatekeeping mechanism. When fans defend Patrick, they aren't just defending a photo; they are pushing back against a culture that demands perfection from players while allowing the game to become overly serious.

The sport needs to remember that it is a game, not a religious service. If a group is not actually delaying the pace of play, why does a moment of joy need to be scrutinized so heavily? The double standard regarding gender and celebration remains a persistent problem that the PGA Tour and local clubs should address more openly.

title: NY Knicks talks with Karl-Anthony Towns reportedly stalled over ‘unreasonable’ $76 million paycut
description: Karl-Anthony Towns and the New York Knicks have been trying to come to terms on a new contract, but find themselves far apart at the negotiation table. Towns has proven himself to be a valuable figure for the Knicks, having helped the Knicks win their first NBA championship in 53 years.
fullText:
Karl-Anthony Towns and the New York Knicks have been trying to come to terms on a new contract, but find themselves far apart at the negotiation table.

Towns has proven himself to be a valuable figure for the Knicks, having helped the Knicks win their first NBA championship in 53 years.

But the Knicks find themselves struggling with the strict salary cap rules, which is why they haven't been able to agree to a new deal with the All-Star center.

According to Jake Fischer, the New York Knicks would prefer that Karl-Anthony Towns sign a four-year, $200 million extension with the team.

This would be much less than the $276 million contract extension that Towns is eligible to sign to stay with the Knicks.

Malika Andrews of ESPN reported separately that Towns was willing to take a pay cut, but one that would be reasonable.

"Karl-Anthony Towns, from what I have been told, is willing, similarly to what Jalen Brunson did. Numbers aren't the same, but he is also willing to take a pay cut. But the pay cut that the Knicks are asking him to take, he views as unreasonable."

Both these reports suggest that the Knicks front office and Towns are struggling to come to terms on a new contract extension.

From Towns' perspective, he is well within his rights to hold out and maximise his salary, given what he helped the Knicks accomplish last season.

And even if there is talk of him taking slightly less money, KAT is unwilling to sacrifice too much of his salary just to help the team.

Towns is currently in the final year of the four-year, $220 million contract he signed with the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Even though he has a $61 million player option for the 2027-28 NBA season, Towns would like to have a long-term contract extension secured with the Knicks.

The Knicks, for their part, are trying to keep their championship core together while complying with the NBA's salary cap rules.

Hopefully, the extension talks continue, and the two sides can come to an agreement over a new deal, as Towns is too important to the Knicks.

title: Luis Figo urges Mourinho to give Real Madrid summer signing a bigger role: ‘Has a lot of technical quality’
description: Real Madrid made several important signings in the summer, but some of them have had a mixed start to life at the Santiago Bernabeu.Bernardo Silva arrived from Manchester City on a free transfer, and ...
fullText:
Real Madrid made several important signings in the summer, but some of them have had a mixed start to life at the Santiago Bernabeu.

Bernardo Silva arrived from Manchester City on a free transfer, and the Portuguese midfielder has not made a particularly strong start for Los Blancos.

Madrid icon Luis Figo believes Silva can provide Real Madrid with an important quality they have sometimes lacked in midfield this season.

As quoted by Defensa Central, Figo believes Bernardo's technical ability could help Madrid improve their build-up in possession.

"Bernardo Silva has a lot of technical quality," Figo said.

"If Mourinho decides to give him more minutes, he will surely provide that quality in the construction of the game, which is one of his strengths."

Mourinho's side are six points behind Barcelona following their derby defeat to Atletico Madrid, with their midfield balance raising question marks.

Bernardo Silva has received fewer minutes than initially anticipated. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images)

Bernardo has so far received fewer minutes than might have been expected when he arrived from Manchester City.

His profile is different from the other Los Blancos options. Fede Valverde, Aurelien Tchouameni and Eduardo Camavinga offer enormous physical and defensive qualities, but Bernardo is the natural controller.

What Silva brings to the table is distinctive, and Mourinho needs to start giving him more minutes in the coming weeks.

He came off the bench against Atletico Madrid and, despite Madrid being down to 10 men, helped them enjoy their best spell of the game.

Bernardo may not have started brightly in the Spanish capital, but there is no doubting his quality or what he can add to this team.

Bernardo Silva is likely to find more prominence in the team after the break. (Photo by David Balogh/Getty Images)

With Fede Valverde out injured, there could be a window of opportunity for the Portuguese midfielder to impress immediately after the international break.

So far, Mourinho has preferred using Tchouameni and Valverde as his first-choice midfield pairing in important games.

However, the strengths of both players tend to overlap more than they complement each other, and Silva could help address this.

The next few weeks should provide more clarity on whether Silva's prominence in the team improves, and it remains to be seen how the situation pans out.

title: Rob Gronkowski issues out ‘advice’ after what he’s seen from Fernando Mendoza
description: Rob Gronkowski knows exactly what it takes to remain financially responsible as an NFL player. The future Hall of Fame tight end has previously discussed how he never touched a penny of his NFL earnings during his playing career, as he lived off brand deals.
fullText:
Rob Gronkowski knows exactly what it takes to remain financially responsible as an NFL player.

The future Hall of Fame tight end has previously discussed how he never touched a penny of his NFL earnings during his playing career, as he lived off brand deals.

Rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza has now been involved in a unique partnership sharing financial advice for others.

The feedback on the promo for the campaign has been largely positive, with Mendoza promoting an ethical topic.

However, Gronkowski has issued the Las Vegas Raiders backup quarterback some advice until he does secure the starting spot over Kirk Cousins.

Mendoza has been working with the U.S. Bank to help Gen Z fans manage their finances in a more responsible manner.

Gronkowski was and still is the face of numerous advertising campaigns, which makes him the perfect person to share some advice with Mendoza.

"This guy could be out in Las Vegas. He could be out at the clubs. He's not doing any of that. He's trying to be the best possible football player that he could be. The reason why he's not playing right now is because Kirk Cousins is playing, and Fernando's learning behind him. Fernando's going to be super ready when it's his time to shine," said Gronkowski.

"Fernando as well. I feel like he's quirky enough to be able to pull off one of those videos, but my only advice is: yes, you have a lot of success with that promo, Fernando. Just don't keep putting out different promos for different companies.

"Yes, that one was great, but hey, just stick to that one. Once you start playing, more will come down the road. Don't be shooting out promos left and right with companies until you start playing and get on the field."

The Raiders take on the Kansas City Chiefs this weekend, with one of the teams set to lose their unbeaten record.

What Klint Kubiak has seen from Cousins has been seriously impressive, with very little room provided from the veteran for Mendoza to stake a claim as the starter.

For now, the first overall pick will have to watch from the sidelines and learn from his 38-year-old superior.

title: Ravens vs. Titans: Five early matchups to watch in Week 4
description: Coaching battles, Derrick Henry's attachment to both teams, and personnel matchups highlight Ravens vs. Titans.
fullText:
The Baltimore Ravens and Tennessee Titans have a competitive history. The two franchises have met 27 times, with Baltimore holding a narrow 14-13 advantage. They've won each of the past two meetings. They meet this coming Sunday in Week 4. This week's matchup carries a few extra storylines.

Derrick Henry faces the organization where he spent the first eight seasons of his career, while both teams enter the game looking to build momentum after dramatically different starts to the season. Coaching will play a significant role in determining the outcome, but several individual matchups deserve attention as well. Here are some early thoughts about some matchups worth watching

One of the game's most respected defensive minds squares off against a rising offensive play-caller who continues to grow into his role. Robert Saleh has built a reputation around aggressive, disciplined defenses that force offenses to execute consistently. Declan Doyle, meanwhile, has already shown creativity and adaptability despite calling plays for the first time in his career.

Doyle's offense has experienced some early growing pains, but it has also produced explosive plays and found ways to put points on the board. The challenge this week will be finding answers against a defensive coach who has spent years making life difficult for opposing quarterbacks and offensive coordinators. This matchup feels like a fascinating chess match between experience and innovation.

The Titans' offense will test a Ravens defense that is still searching for consistency. Jesse Minter handles play-calling responsibilities, while Anthony Weaver remains heavily involved in game-planning and in-game adjustments. Together, they are working to establish Baltimore's defensive identity under a new coaching staff.

Across the field in the Titans' booth sits Brian Daboll, one of the NFL's most respected offensive architects. Questions have followed him since his departure from Buffalo, with some wondering how much of his success was tied to Josh Allen's development.

Tennessee's offense remains a work in progress, but Daboll can still create favorable matchups and stress a defense's communication. This battle may ultimately determine whether the Ravens can control the game's pace.

Both sides enter this matchup looking for answers. Ward has endured a difficult start to his professional career, but the Titans have surrounded him with capable pass catchers. Gunnar Helm has emerged as a reliable tight end target, while Calvin Ridley, Carnell Tate, and Wan'Dale Robinson provide speed and playmaking ability on the perimeter.

Baltimore's secondary has experienced its share of ups and downs through three weeks. Communication breakdowns and explosive plays have surfaced at unfortunate moments, making this an important test for a veteran defensive backfield.

On paper, the Ravens have the advantage. The challenge will be translating that advantage into consistent execution.

This may be the most important matchup of the game. The Dallas Cowboys generated more pressure than many expected and repeatedly won critical short-yardage situations against Baltimore. The Ravens surrendered a goal-line stand, struggled in some fourth-down situations, and left several opportunities on the field.

Now comes an even tougher challenge. Jeffery Simmons, John Franklin-Myers, and Jermaine Johnson headline a Tennessee front capable of disrupting both the running and passing games. Anthony Hill Jr. serves as the centerpiece of the defense and has quickly become one of the Titans' most productive defenders.

If Baltimore's offensive line controls the line of scrimmage, the Ravens should have opportunities to dictate the game. If Tennessee wins up front, things could become much more complicated.

The quarterback matchup offers an interesting contrast. Lamar Jackson entered the NFL as the final first-round selection in a quarterback class that included Baker Mayfield, Sam Darnold, Josh Allen, and Josh Rosen. Since then, he has become one of the league's most accomplished players and remains the standard in the AFC North.

Ward arrived with a different level of pre-draft attention as the first overall pick in 2025. He is still working through the growing pains that often accompany young quarterbacks, and at times the speed of the NFL game seems challenging.

The Titans believe Ward can eventually become the face of their franchise. On Sunday, he will be measured against one of the league's premier quarterbacks.

Few storylines are easier to appreciate than this one. Henry spent eight seasons carrying Tennessee's offense before joining Baltimore. Now he faces a Titans defense that enters Week 4 ranked 24th against the run, allowing 126.3 rushing yards per game.

The Ravens have made it clear that Henry remains a focal point of their offense. He enters the game with six rushing touchdowns through three weeks and remains Baltimore's most reliable scoring threat near the goal line.

Tennessee knows Henry's strengths better than almost anyone. The question is whether that familiarity will help slow him down. If Baltimore establishes the running game early, the Ravens could force the Titans into a long afternoon and create favorable opportunities for Jackson and the passing attack.

title: Padres' Michael King delivers October masterpiece in Game 1 rout of Cubs
description: What a masterpiece from the Padres starting pitcher on Tuesday.
fullText:
Padres' Michael King delivers October masterpiece in Game 1 rout of Cubs originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The San Diego Padres have plenty of recognizable stars.

Michael King stole the show Tuesday night. King delivered seven scoreless innings as San Diego overwhelmed the Chicago Cubs 8-0 in Game 1 of their National League Wild Card Series.

He allowed just one hit. King struck out eight, walked three and threw 97 pitches while putting the Padres one victory away from advancing.

Short postseason series can turn on one mistake. King barely made any. Chicago couldn't establish anything offensively against the San Diego right-hander, who kept the Cubs scoreless long enough for the Padres lineup to take control.

Fernando Tatis Jr.: 2-for-3, HR, SB, 3 R
Manny Machado: 2B, HR, 2 RBI
Michael King: 7 IP, 1 H, 0 R, 8 Ks

The @Padres dominate Game 1!

(MLB x @AbbVie) pic.twitter.com/sPynbBfJwm

Fernando Tatis Jr., Manny Machado and Xander Bogaerts all homered.

Tatis scored three times, while Jackson Merrill also contributed a two-run single as San Diego broke open the game.

It was the kind of complete performance that immediately changes the tone of a best-of-three series. The Padres didn't merely win. They controlled virtually every phase of the opener.

MORE: Yankees' Cam Schlittler sends message after dominant playoff performance vs. Red Sox

That's what should concern Chicago most entering Game 2. San Diego didn't need one superstar to carry the lineup.

Tatis homered. Machado homered. Bogaerts homered. Merrill delivered with runners aboard. And King prevented the Cubs from creating any meaningful response.

There was another encouraging development for San Diego, too.

Joe Musgrove pitched in relief, marking his first major league appearance since the 2024 postseason after undergoing Tommy John surgery. Musgrove helped complete the shutout alongside Yuki Matsui.

Now comes the difficult part. The Padres must finish the job.

Wild Card Series can change quickly, and Chicago gets another opportunity Wednesday night. But San Diego couldn't have created a better opening statement.

King dominated. The stars produced. The bullpen finished it. And after an 8-0 victory, the Padres need just one more win to move deeper into October.

title: Drawing of lots sends Oman through to Gulf Cup semis
description: Oman edge into the semi-finals of the Gulf Cup but they do so in extraordinary fashion after they are picked ahead of Iraq in the drawing of lots.
fullText:
Oman edged into the semi-finals of the Gulf Cup in extraordinary fashion after they were picked ahead of Iraq in the drawing of lots.

Oman's 3-1 win over Kuwait meant both the Omanis and Iraq finished level on four points in their group and, as they had identical records, lots were drawn to separate them and decide who would finish second and progress to the last four.

Organisers said the draw was the final tie-breaker after they had applied "the selection criteria stipulated in the regulations".

These included "head-to-head results, goal difference, number of goals, and disciplinary card points" with Oman and Iraq level "until the final criterion was reached".

With yellow cards included in the count-back categories, Oman's Musab Al-Shaqsy would have been ruing the booking he picked up against Kuwait.

After Al-Shaqsy scored his side's third goal late on in their win over Iraq he was yellow carded for taking his top off during his celebration.

And, with Oman and Iran, who were beaten 2-0 by Saudi Arabia in their final group game, level on everything else, it meant both countries also finished even on the disciplinary front.

That meant lots had to be drawn "in the presence of representatives of the concerned authorities" and, ultimately, Oman went through to the semi-finals.

One of the most recent cases of a drawing of lots occurred at the Africa Cup of Nations in 2015.

On that occasion, Guinea progressed to the quarter-finals at the expense of Mali after both had finished level in their group.

At the 1990 World Cup in Italy, the Netherlands and the Republic of Ireland were tied in their group and, while both were guaranteed a place in the next round, lots were needed to determine who would qualify in second and who would qualify in third place.

The draw resulted in Ireland being awarded second place and a game against Romania, while the Dutch ended up third and faced eventual winners West Germany.

In 1970, lots were required during the World Cup to determine who out of the Soviet Union and Mexico would be named group winners of Group One. The Soviet Union ended up being deemed group winners.

Although it had not been needed since 1994 the drawing of lots remained as the final tie-breaker until the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, after which it was replaced by where the teams stand in the latest Fifa world rankings, which are updated after every international match.

title: Ireland to host England at Aviva Stadium in Six Nations
description: Ireland's 2027 Women's Six Nations encounter with England will be played at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.
fullText:
Ireland's 2027 Women's Six Nations encounter with England will be played at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

Scott Bemand's side made their Six Nations debut at the Aviva Stadium with a win over Scotland in this year's competition and will welcome the world champions to Dublin in the fourth round of fixtures on 8 May.

A crowd of 31,294 watched the 54-5 win over Scotland in May, a record crowd for a women's match in Ireland.

"Playing at Aviva Stadium last season was an incredible and landmark experience for the group and we're really excited to be returning to the home of Irish rugby in 2027," said Ireland captain Erin King.

"These are the occasions you want to be involved in as a player and with two big home matches against France and England coming up in 2027, there is huge motivation for us as a group to produce the occasions and performances that will inspire and excite our Green Wave."

Bemand's side open their campaign in Scotland at Murrayfield on 10 April before they welcome France to the Dexcom Stadium in Galway for their other home fixture of the competition.

Ireland are back on the road in Wales before the Red Roses come to Dublin for the highly anticipated penultimate fixture.

Italy then host the Irish on the final weekend on 15 May.

Ireland finished third in the 2026 Six Nations behind England, who have been champions for the past eight years, and France.

title: UCLA Bruins' ascent makes the Trojans' situation a lot worse
description: Lincoln Riley cannot afford another disappointing season for all the obvious reasons. A new one: The UCLA Bruins are rising under Bob Chesney
fullText:
The USC Trojans' struggles have been frustrating to see, and the season is already looking grim. To make matters worse, another former Pac-12 rival is in contention for a College Football Playoff berth from the Big Ten. That's UCLA. The Bruins are rising while the Trojans do not look the part.

In a recent tweet, writer Bryan Fischer highlights just how frustrating things have been at USC under Lincoln Riley. Here is what he had to say:

"UCLA has improved 

The UCLA Bruins have been night-and-day better than last year's team. Even when things got better late in the season, the Bruins are still a much better team than last year. What Bob Chesney has done over there is just another example that if the right coach comes in, it does not take long to see the impact. Chesney is even getting comparisons to Curt Cignetti.

With Riley at USC, it has been years without any true elevation. The standard for Riley at USC has been postseason success and making the College Football Playoff. The Trojans are still far from that. USC has also gotten spanked by its rival, the Oregon Ducks, for 5 straight games. Its rival has been one of the best teams in the Big Ten, while USC is still fighting to prove it's worthy of being in the conference.

It is very fitting that the UCLA Bruins are able to overcome a disastrous season and look more promising than the Trojans, who came into the year with high expectations. Lincoln Riley is in desperate need of righting the ship at USC before the season takes another turn for the worse.

title: Why Jason Kelce apologized during ESPN broadcast after Pat McAfee callout
description: Jason Kelce got called out by Pat McAfee and apologized on ESPN. Here's why.
fullText:
Jason Kelce is a Philadelphia Eagles legend, a player who will be one of the all-time most beloved members of the franchise. But Kelce knew he made a mistake on Monday night while he was part of the Monday Night Football crew.

While at halftime and breaking down the eventual Eagles loss at the time, Kelce broke down what Philly was doing and referred to them as "we" as if he was still a member of the Eagles.

Pat McAfee next to him remarked, "A lot of 'we' talk out of Jason from Philly," and Kelce was quick to say he was "sorry" as he tried to stay neutral with his analysis.

Jason Kelce had to apologize on TV for constantly referring to the Eagles as, “We.” 😂 🦅 pic.twitter.com/pbdlbzkIGx

No big deal, and frankly, if anyone can say "we" about the Eagles these days while not being on the roster, it's Kelce. And that's something Ryan Clark noted on X (formerly Twitter).

I’m trying to mind my own , but hell yea it’s “We” Future Hall of Famer!! You’re a legend @JasonKelce. Blood, sweat, tears, & glory in Philly. No one can take that away. 

You can still do your job the right way! Bump anyone saying differently.
